text:
Matty Beniers has goals in three straight games and 7 on the season, five in his last ten. Alison Lukan, covering the Kraken, noted the chemistry on his line after a 5-1 win over Vancouver, a seven-shot night for Beniers. For a former Calder Trophy winner who has spent three years being measured against his rookie season, this is the version Seattle hoped for.

Some of it is real. He has 13 points in 20 games at 17:56 a night, and Seattle's 5v5 numbers are better with him on the ice than off. Some of it is the bounces. He's shooting 23.3% on 30 shots, well above his likely range of 12% to 17%, with 7 goals on 5.0 expected (the quality of his chances). His team has also scored 3 more goals than its chances deserve with him on.

Evolving-Hockey found the same pattern last season: results ahead of chances. The chances themselves (0.84 expected goals per 60) are close to what he's always made. So enjoy the streak, but the useful thing to watch is the shot count. Thirty shots in 20 games won't hold a 23% conversion rate for long.
headline: Beniers is scoring, a little too easily
